overview: After 1.b4 e5 2.Bb2 f6 White plays 3.e4, leaving b4 en prise to ...Bxb4. Black takes the pawn and White follows with Bc4, f4 and f5 to attack the weakened kingside, as in the Brinckmann line 4.Bc4 Nc6 5.f4 Qe7 6.f5 g6.

white_ideas.idea: Bc4, f4 and f5 on the kingside
Use the Bb2 against the weak long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: Black f6 pawn weakens e6 and g6; White pawns on e4 and f4

character.notes: Open lines and a weakened Black king.

gambit.notes: b4 can be taken with ...Bxb4 and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Compensation is real but not clearly enough; playable.

level.notes: Needs concrete knowledge of the attack.

sublines_that_differ.name: Brinckmann Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. b4 e5 2. Bb2 f6 3. e4 Bxb4 4. Bc4 Nc6 5. f4 Qe7 6. f5 g6
sublines_that_differ.how: White pushes f5 immediately to open lines against the king.

character.reason: A gambit with early attack and open lines.

gambit.reason: White offers b4, and ...Bxb4 wins a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Compensation is real but Black's extra pawn makes it a close call.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off and the pieces play on open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the Tartakower Gambit.

level.reason: Needs concrete play, but not heavy theory.

plans.reason: White plays Bc4, f4 and f5 against the kingside.
